items.statement: Adani Power experienced significant revenue growth due to higher volumes, improved realizations, strong power demand, and increased operating capacity.
items.quote: Higher volumes and improved realization following strong growth in power demand along with higher operating capacity, leading to handsome growth in revenues

items.statement: Fuel costs increased due to higher volumes and rising import fuel prices driven by geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East.
items.quote: Fuel cost increase due to higher volumes and increase in import fuel prices following energy market disruptions due to the geopolitical situation in the Middle East

items.statement: Operating expenses rose as a result of the company's expanding scale and recent acquisitions.
items.quote: Higher operating expenses in line with growth in scale and recent acquisitions

items.statement: The government is increasing investments in thermal and renewable energy to satisfy growing demand from manufacturing, infrastructure, e-mobility, and digitalization.
items.quote: Government boosting thermal and renewable investments to meet rising demand from manufacturing, infrastructure, e-mobility & digitalization

items.statement: States are inviting competitive bids for long-term thermal power supply under the SHAKTI policy based on Resource Adequacy Reports.
items.quote: Coal allocations to states under SHAKTI policy for inviting competitive bids for Long-term thermal power supply based on Resource Adequacy Reports

items.statement: The company targets a nuclear power capacity of 10 GW by 2035, with project sites already identified.
items.quote: Targeting capacity of 10 GW by 2035; sites identified for project location

items.statement: Adani Power is expanding its thermal power capacity by 23.7 GW with an estimated capex of ₹ 2 Trillion, targeting completion by FY 2031-32.
items.quote: Ongoing capacity expansion of 23.7 GW thermal power plants with estimated capex of ₹ 2 Trillion and targeted completion by FY 2031-32

items.statement: A strong revival in power demand and a spike in peak demand have led to improved offtake under PPAs.
items.quote: Strong revival in power demand and spike in peak demand leading to improved offtake under PPAs

items.statement: Above-normal temperatures, frequent heatwaves, and delayed rainfall in Summer 2026 led to a spike in power demand across India after slow growth in 2025.
items.quote: Above-normal temperatures in Summer 2026 with frequent heatwaves and delayed rainfall over large parts of India, leading to spike in demand for power after slow growth in 2025.

items.statement: All-India power demand grew by 8.4% in Q1 FY27 compared to Q1 FY26, with peak demand crossing 270 GW in May 2026 during solar hours.
items.quote: Peak demand crosses 270 GW in May 2026 during solar hours and 248 GW during non-solar hours, while all-India power demand grew by 8.4% during Q1 FY27 vs Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Higher dispatch volumes and improved realisations resulted in significant growth in continuing revenue.
items.quote: Higher dispatch volumes and improved realisations lead to handsome growth in Continuing Revenue

items.statement: Fuel costs rose because of higher volumes and increased import fuel prices caused by geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East.
items.quote: Fuel cost increase due to higher volumes and increase in import fuel prices following energy market disruptions due to the geopolitical situation in the Middle East

items.statement: EBITDA grew strongly in line with volume growth and improved realization, highlighting the company's core earnings strength.
items.quote: Strong growth in EBITDA in line with volume growth and improved realization, emphasizing core earnings strength

items.statement: The company is expanding its thermal power capacity by 23.7 GW with an estimated capex of ₹ 2 Trillion, targeting completion by FY 2031-32.
items.quote: Ongoing capacity expansion of 23.7 GW thermal power plants with estimated capex of ₹ 2 Trillion and targeted completion by FY 2031-32

items.statement: The first project of 570 MW will be established under SPV Wangchhu Hydroelectric Power Ltd. with an estimated cost of ₹ 60 Billion.
items.quote: First project of 570 MW to be set up under SPV Wangchhu Hydroelectric Power Ltd. with 49:51 stake of APL and DGPC; estimated project cost of ₹ 60 Billion

items.statement: The company's capital expenditure is largely self-funded, and prudent debt management helps maintain high creditworthiness.
items.quote: Largely self-funded capital expenditure and prudent debt management helping maintain high creditworthiness

items.statement: Adani Power is executing an ongoing capacity expansion of 23.7 GW of thermal power plants, targeted for completion by FY 2031-32.
items.quote: Ongoing capacity expansion of 23.7 GW thermal power plants with estimated capex of ₹ 2 Trillion and targeted completion by FY 2031-32

items.statement: Adani Power is partnering with Bhutan's Druk Green Power Corporation to develop 5 GW of hydroelectric power capacity to supply power to both nations.
items.quote: Development of 5 GW hydroelectric power capacity in Bhutan in partnership with the Govt of Bhutan’s Druk Green Power Corporation for supply of power to both countries

items.statement: The company was awarded a 625 MW long-term PPA by Karnataka DISCOM and a 3,200 MW long-term PPA by Assam DISCOM.
items.quote: Includes 625 MW long term PPA awarded by Karnataka DISCOM and 3,200 MW long term PPA awarded by Assam DISCOM

items.statement: Out of 19.3 GW of PPAs awarded by states in the last two financial years, Adani Power won bids for 12.6 GW.
items.quote: States have awarded 19.3 GW PPAs in last two financial years, of which APL has won bids for 12.6 GW

items.statement: Strong operating profitability and controlled leverage have led to high earnings conversion and solid PAT performance.
items.quote: Robust operating profitability and control on leverage leading to high conversion and solid PAT performance

items.statement: An effectively unlevered capital structure provides Adani Power with significant free cash flow to equity.
items.quote: Effectively unlevered capital structure provides APL with significant free cashflow to equity

items.statement: Adani Power acquired the power assets of Jaiprakash Associates Ltd., including a 180 MW power plant in Churk, Uttar Pradesh, for ₹ 4,194 Crore.
items.quote: Power assets of Jaiprakash Associates Ltd. (Q1 FY 2026-27) 180 MW power plant in Churk (Uttar Pradesh) Acquisition value ₹ 4,194 Crore

items.statement: Adani Power established a wholly owned subsidiary, Adani Atomic Energy Ltd., to invest in nuclear power opportunities to meet the growing national demand for clean energy.
items.quote: APL has set up a wholly owned subsidiary, Adani Atomic Energy Ltd., to invest in the emerging opportunity of nuclear power to serve the growing national demand for clean, round-the-clock power.

items.statement: India requires an additional 97 GW of thermal capacity by 2035 to satisfy its growing base load and peak demand.
items.quote: 97 GW of additional thermal capacity needed by 2035 to meet India’s growing base load and peak demand

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East present risks to fuel costs by causing energy market disruptions and increasing import fuel prices.
items.quote: Fuel cost increase due to higher volumes and increase in import fuel prices following energy market disruptions due to the geopolitical situation in the Middle East

items.statement: positive
items.quote: Strong portfolio of operating assets, locked-in capacity and further growth opportunities

items.statement: Adani Power achieved its highest ever quarterly power generation of 31 billion units and dispatched 28.8 billion units, representing a 17% growth.
items.quote: We achieved our highest ever quarterly power generation of 31 billion units and dispatched 28.8 billion units, a growth of 17%, which was a result of improved PLF as well as greater operating capacity.

items.statement: The company's profit after tax for the first quarter of FY27 increased by 47% year-on-year to INR 4,867 crores.
items.quote: The company has reported 47% higher profit after tax on year-on-year at INR4,867 crores for quarter 1 FY27, reflecting our operational profitability and excellent management of the capital structure.

items.statement: The consolidated plant load factor increased to 78% in the first quarter of FY27 from 67% in the same quarter of the previous year.
items.quote: Our consolidated plant load factor jumped significantly to 78% in quarter 1 FY '27 compared to 67% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Fuel costs for the quarter increased by 30% to INR 9,513 crores due to higher dispatch volumes and increased imported coal indices.
items.quote: The Fuel cost for the quarter was higher by 30% at INR9,513 crores, which was driven by larger dispatch volumes and higher imported imported coal indices.

items.statement: Management expects revenues and EBITDA to remain stable over the near and medium term due to supplying power mostly under long-term contracts.
items.quote: But now that we largely are supplying power under long-term contracts, we expect to see over the near term and medium term, typically more of stability when it comes to revenues and EBITDA.

items.statement: Management expects the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to remain between 2 and 3 and not exceed 3 at any point.
items.quote: We are expecting that net debt-to-EBITDA will not cross 3 times at any point. So this net debt to EBITDA level of between 2 to 3 will persist over this period of time.

items.statement: The company expects its expansion capex to be approximately INR 25,000 crores this year, INR 33,000 crores next year, and over INR 35,000 crores thereafter.
items.quote: This year, we are expecting that our expansion CapEx will be near about INR25,000 crores. Next year, it will be near about INR33,000 crores, and thereafter it will be more than INR35,000 crores.

items.statement: The company has revised its capacity target from 42 GW to 45 GW by the same timeline.
items.quote: Now our target is 45 GW by the same time. It is now revised from 42 to 45. And we are confident that we'll be able to achieve it.

items.statement: Peak power demand reached a record high of approximately 271 GW in May 2026, with overall energy consumption increasing by 8.4% year-on-year in the first quarter of FY27.
items.quote: Due to these high temperatures, peak demand shot up to a record high of around 271 GW in May '26, while overall energy consumption rose by 8.4% on a year-on-year to 485 billion units for quarter 1, FY27.

items.statement: High demand led to a significant improvement in power offtake under power purchase agreements and a material strengthening of merchant prices.
items.quote: Consequently, power offtake under PPAs improved significantly, while merchant prices also strengthened materially.

items.statement: Tariff realizations under power purchase agreements rose by 8% to INR 5.93 per unit, while merchant and short-term realizations increased by 13% to INR 7.04 per unit.
items.quote: Our tariff realization under PPA improved by 8% to INR5.93 per unit and merchant and short-term realization improved by 13% to INR7.04 per unit, directly benefiting from the strong demand environment.

items.statement: Fuel costs rose by 30% to INR 9,513 crores, driven by increased dispatch volumes and higher imported coal indices.
items.quote: The Fuel cost for the quarter was higher by 30% at INR9,513 crores, which was driven by larger dispatch volumes and higher imported imported coal indices.

items.statement: The company plans to spend approximately INR 25,000 crores on expansion capex this year, INR 33,000 crores next year, and more than INR 35,000 crores in the following years.
items.quote: This year, we are expecting that our expansion CapEx will be near about INR25,000 crores. Next year, it will be near about INR33,000 crores, and thereafter it will be more than INR35,000 crores.

items.statement: The company is on schedule to commission the 1,320 MW Korba Phase-II project this year and the 1,600 MW Mahan Phase-II project in the first quarter of the next financial year.
items.quote: We are on track to commission the 1,320 MW Korba Phase-II project this year, while the 1,600-MW Mahan Phase-II project is scheduled for commercial operation in quarter 1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Construction progress has exceeded 62% at Raipur Phase-II and 54% at Raigarh Phase-II, while execution has started on the 1,600 MW Mirzapur greenfield project.
items.quote: Furthermore, execution is advancing rapidly at Raipur Phase-II and Raigarh Phase-II, which have achieved over 62% and 54% progress, respectively, and we have commenced execution for our 1,600-MW Mirzapur greenfield project and other projects.

items.statement: The company expects the Korba Phase-II project to be commissioned before the end of December this year.
items.quote: We expect that Korba Phase-II will come before December end this year. That is the broader expectation.

items.statement: The company signed a 25-year power supply agreement with the Maharashtra DISCOM to supply 1,600 MW of power from an ultra-supercritical thermal power plant.
items.quote: Additionally, we secured our revenue visibility further by signing a 25-year power supply agreement with the Maharashtra DISCOM for supply of 1,600 MW of power on a long-term basis from a 2x800-MW Ultra-Supercritical thermal power plant.

items.statement: As of June 30, 2026, the company's total outstanding debt was INR 58,381 crores, and its net debt was INR 47,643 crores.
items.quote: As of June 30, '26, our total debt outstanding stood at INR58,381 crores, and our net debt stood at INR47,643 crores.

items.statement: The company's current net debt-to-EBITDA ratio is slightly above 2 times, and it is expected to remain below 3 times.
items.quote: Net debt-to-EBITDA as on date, is slightly higher than 2 timex. We are expecting that net debt-to-EBITDA will not cross 3 times at any point.

items.statement: The company expanded its portfolio by acquiring the 180 MW Churk power plant, a 24% stake in Jaiprakash Power Ventures, and an 11.49% stake in Prayagraj Power Generation Company.
items.quote: This strategic move adds 180-MW Churk power plant to our portfolio, alongside a 24% stake in Jaiprakash Power Ventures and an 11.49% stake in Prayagraj Power Generation Company.

items.statement: The company is expanding its thermal base while diversifying into international hydropower projects and preparing for opportunities in nuclear power.
items.quote: Looking beyond the horizon, we are entering new and exciting territories as we expand our thermal base, we are also diversifying into international hydropower projects and preparing ourselves for new opportunities in the nuclear power field.

items.statement: Reliable baseload power has become increasingly important for India's economic growth as the country's economy continues to advance.
items.quote: As India's economy continues to advance, the importance of reliable baseload power for the country's growth story has become even more evident.

items.statement: Thermal power served as the primary source for meeting India's electricity requirements during a period of high demand.
items.quote: Thermal power was once again the mainstay for fulfilling the nation's electricity needs during this period of surging demand.

items.statement: The company aims to secure medium- or long-term power purchase agreements for almost all of its capacity to mitigate the volatility of merchant prices.
items.quote: We have earlier said that going forward, we would like to tie up almost everything through medium term or long term PPAs to reduce volatility inherent in merchant prices.
